articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine In a fifteen-second recording donated to a public corpus, a woman is saying something ordinary in Vietnamese. When she stops talking, one of the two speech models I ran over it hears nothing at all — and the other thanks an audience that isn't there: "Cảm ơn các bạn đã chào tạm biệt và hẹn gặp lại trong video tiếp theo." Thanks for watching, see you in the next video. She never made a video. That sentence is why this project exists. The recording I actually care about is the one nobody has made yet: a grandmother naming which ancestors get a giỗ, and on which lunar day, while someone finally thinks to press record. Her pauses will be longer than that woman's.

articles.title: Freelancer vs Agency for SaaS Development: A Founder's Decision Framework
articles.excerpt: "Should I hire a freelancer or an agency?" is usually the wrong first question. The right first question is what you actually need: one accountable person who can move fast on a narrow, well-defined b…
articles.body: "Should I hire a freelancer or an agency?" is usually the wrong first question. The right first question is what you actually need: one accountable person who can move fast on a narrow, well-defined build, or a team that can absorb more scope, more specialties, and more risk at once. Both freelancers and agencies can build a good SaaS product. Both can also leave you with a half-finished one. The difference rarely comes down to talent — it comes down to whether the engagement model matches your stage, your scope, and how much risk you can personally absorb if something goes wrong. This guide compares the two options on the dimensions that actually predict project outcomes: accountability, capacity, cost drivers, and stage fit.

articles.title: I Built a Chrome Audio Recorder Extension — Meet Pulse
articles.excerpt: Recording audio from a browser tab sounds like a simple task. Open an extension, click Record, and save the file. But what happens when you pause a video, need to record several tabs, or your browser…
articles.body: Recording audio from a browser tab sounds like a simple task. Open an extension, click Record, and save the file. But what happens when you pause a video, need to record several tabs, or your browser crashes after two hours of recording? These are some of the problems I wanted to address when I started developing Pulse , a Chrome extension for recording audio directly from browser tabs. Before building it, I spent time reading reviews of existing audio recording extensions in the Chrome Web Store. I was particularly interested in negative reviews and feature requests: what frustrated users, what made recording unnecessarily complicated, and what they wished their recorders could do automatically. That research helped shape Pulse.

articles.title: Stop Overengineering Your Side Projects: A Practical Guide to App Architecture
articles.excerpt: You don't need microservices, Kubernetes, and 15 cloud services to launch your next SaaS product. If you're a solo developer, you're already wearing multiple hats: Frontend Developer Backend Developer…
articles.body: You don't need microservices, Kubernetes, and 15 cloud services to launch your next SaaS product. If you're a solo developer, you're already wearing multiple hats: Frontend Developer Backend Developer Database Administrator DevOps Engineer Security Engineer And occasionally, the person debugging production at 2 AM. 😅 The last thing you need is an architecture that creates more work than your actual product. The Architecture Trap It's tempting to design applications the way Netflix, Uber, or Amazon would. But here's the thing: You're not building for millions of users on Day 1. You're building to get your first 10. For most solo developers, a modular monolith is a better starting point than microservices. One application. Clear boundaries. Fewer moving parts.

articles.title: Two PyTorch ops that stopped a CUDA text model on an Apple GPU
articles.excerpt: The Next-Concept Modeling eval scripts would not start on this Mac. PyTorch 2.14.1 reported the Apple GPU as available, and evaluate.py still exited with no GPU visible; pass --gpus. The model itself…
articles.body: The Next-Concept Modeling eval scripts would not start on this Mac. PyTorch 2.14.1 reported the Apple GPU as available, and evaluate.py still exited with no GPU visible; pass --gpus . The model itself did not need a rewrite. The released configs already turn FlexAttention off and use scaled dot-product attention, linear layers, embeddings, and RoPE. Three call sites assumed CUDA. Two of those assumptions are real Metal limits, and the third is just device plumbing. The launcher only counted CUDA devices evaluate.py asked torch.cuda.device_count() and then set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES for each shard. On a Mac that count is zero, so the process stopped before it loaded a checkpoint. A short helper keeps the NVIDIA path and adds the Apple GPU when CUDA is absent: def accelerator () -> torch .

articles.title: Why our AI never writes text on images: a deterministic compositor for 365 branded posts
articles.excerpt: Ask an image model for a poster that says 'Mehta Sweets, Main Market' and you will usually get something close. Close is the problem. For a small business, a post that says 'Mehta Sweats' is worse tha…
articles.body: Ask an image model for a poster that says 'Mehta Sweets, Main Market' and you will usually get something close. Close is the problem. For a small business, a post that says 'Mehta Sweats' is worse than no post at all. And when you generate 365 posts for one shop, 'usually right' means a misspelling somewhere in the year, almost certainly. I build Content365, which makes a whole year of branded social media posts for one Indian small business in one go. Early on we made one rule that shaped everything else: the image model never draws text. Not the name, not the phone number, not the price, not the call to action. This post explains how that works and what it costs us in flexibility. We split the job in two. Each post is built in layers.

articles.title: How 'spacewalking' underwater made me feel like I was really in space
articles.excerpt: Analog Astronaut Commander and Aquanaut Michaela Musilova led underwater simulated “spacewalks” in low visibility to test astronaut safety and communication protocols during simulated space missions.
articles.body: I was breathing just fine through my life support systems, but I kept feeling an urge to double check that everything was ok with my "spacesuit" before heading out on this "spacewalk." I have worn many different types of spacesuits on Earth during my career, but for the first time in my life, I knew that I couldn’t just stop to breathe the air outside if there were an emergency. That's because I was underwater. On this excursion, I was leading a simulated space mission underwater called SEA STAR. My " spacesuit " was actually scuba diving gear, and the simulated spacewalks , or EVAs (Extra-Vehicular Activities), included outings where we explored underwater environments.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
articles.excerpt: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic 'string of pearls,' a unique celestial relic left by a supernova witnessed by humanity around 850 years ago, which has a zombie star at its heart.
articles.body: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago. That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way . What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart. Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf.

articles.title: Cowboy Space unveils 'Big Iron' rocket to launch 20,000 AI data centers
articles.excerpt: Cowboy Space just gave us our first look at its "Big Iron" rocket, which the company will use to build its AI data center constellation. Big Iron's debut is targeted for late 2028.
articles.body: PALO ALTO, Calif. — Cowboy Space just showed us how it plans to become a big player in the final frontier. The California-based company, which is run by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, intends to operate a constellation of 20,000 AI data centers in low Earth orbit (LEO). It will build those satellites in house and launch them on a homegrown rocket — a vehicle Cowboy Space unveiled here on Monday night (Oct. 26), at an event it called "Big Sky Rising." "It's a fundamentally novel approach to rocketry in the modern era, in our opinion," Bhatt said during the event. "The idea is that you have a two-stage rocket where the upper stage of the rocket itself transforms into the satellite." Big Iron's first stage will be reusable.

articles.title: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon
articles.excerpt: Your guide to November's full Beaver Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The November full moon reaches maximum illumination at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk sits opposite the sun in Earth's sky, appearing fully lit by its rays. November's full moon is traditionally known as the " Beaver Moon ", because it rises around the time when the small mammals take refuge in their dens, having stored enough food to survive the long winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . The Nov. 24 full moon also happens to be the first of three consecutive " supermoons ". The non-scientific term is often bestowed on full moons that occur when the natural satellite is within 90% of perigee, when the moon is closest to Earth in its elliptical orbit.
